title: Weak stability of the Gauss fraction field of restricted series
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value. Let $n\ge1$, let $T=k\langle X_1,\ldots,X_nangle$ be the restricted-series ring [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation] with Gauss norm $G(\sum a_
u X^
u)=\sup_
u|a_
u|$, and let $F=\operatorname{Frac}(T)$ carry the Gauss absolute value $|f/g|_F=G(f)/G(g)$. For every finite field extension $E/F$, equip $E$ with the minimal-polynomial spectral norm $s_{E/F}$ [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm]. For every $F$-basis $w_1,\ldots,w_m$ of $E$ there are real constants $c,C>0$ such that $$c\max_i |a_i|_F\ \le\ s_{E/F}\left(\sum_i a_iw_iight)\ \le\ C\max_i|a_i|_F\qquad(a_i\in F).$$ Thus the spectral norm induces the product vector-space topology on each finite extension (weak stability); no exact orthogonal basis, stability of $k$, or separability of $E/F$ is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.1/1 and its proof, printed pp.212–213 (scan PDF pp.218–219); Definition 3.5.2/1, printed p.153 (scan PDF p.161), gives weak stability. The displayed inequalities spell out the weakly cartesian topology for a finite basis. Primary scan read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix a finite extension $E/F$ and an arbitrary $F$-basis $w_1,\ldots,w_m$. The constant embedding $k\hookrightarrow T\hookrightarrow F$ is injective, so $F$ has the same characteristic as $k$, and its absolute value is nontrivial on the constants. If this characteristic is zero, apply [lem-trf-char-zero-spectral-coordinate-topology] with $K=F,L=E$ to obtain exactly the requested two inequalities. No completeness of $F$ is used.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.1/1, first sentence of proof, printed p.212; Proposition 3.5.1/4.

proof.text: Otherwise write $p=\operatorname{char}(k)=\operatorname{char}(F)>0$. In a fixed algebraic closure of $F$ put $T^{1/p}=\{z:z^p\in T\}$, with $N(z)=G(z^p)^{1/p}$. If $M=\sum_{j=1}^r Tm_j\subseteq T^{1/p}$ is finitely generated, its $F$-span is spanned by the same $r$ elements, hence has dimension at most $r$. Thus [lem-trf-tate-root-finite-rank-bseparation] applies to $M$: for every $0\ne x\in M$ it gives a $T$-linear $\lambda:M\to T$ nonzero at $x$ and a bound $G(\lambda(y))\le BN(y)$. This includes the zero module, where there is no nonzero $x$ to check.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.1/1, reduction to Lemma 3.5.3/2 and Lemma 5.3.1/2, printed pp.212-213.

proof.text: First check that $A=T$ with $G$ satisfies the criterion's standing hypotheses. Since $k$ is complete, [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion] shows that $G$ is finite-valued, vanishes exactly at $0$, satisfies $G(1)=1$ and $G(f+g)\le\max(G(f),G(g))$; by [lem-trf-tate-gauss-multiplicative], $G(fg)=G(f)G(g)$. If $fg=0$ with $f,g\ne0$, then $0=G(f)G(g)>0$, a contradiction, so $T$ is an integral domain and $G$ is a real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value on it; on constants it is $|\cdot|$, so $|\cdot|_F$ is nontrivial. Apply [lem-trf-fraction-root-module-weak-stability-criterion] with $A=T$, $K=F$, and the Gauss absolute value. The root ring and its norm are exactly those of step 2, and that step verifies its bounded-separation hypothesis for every finitely generated module. The criterion gives both inequalities for the fixed extension $E/F$ and basis $w_i$, including inseparable extensions. In either characteristic the inequalities imply continuity in both directions between the spectral norm and the coordinate maximum norm, so their open balls induce the same topology. The extension and basis were arbitrary.

BGR is not in the local literature, so I could not open the cited pages (BGR 3.5.1/4, 3.5.2/1, 3.5.3/2, 5.3.1/1–2). The item is correctly marked agent-written with WANTED recorded, and I checked the mathematics myself instead. The split follows BGR's proof of 5.3.1/1: step 1 handles characteristic 0 through lem-trf-char-zero-spectral-coordinate-topology; step 2 shows that a finitely generated M ⊆ T^{1/p} has finite rank, so lem-trf-tate-root-finite-rank-bseparation applies; step 3 applies the criterion lem-trf-fraction-root-module-weak-stability-criterion with A=T and K=F, using the same root norm. Checks: the char-0 node holds by a trace and dual-basis argument, since |Tr y| ≤ max|roots| = s(y); the criterion with a finitely-generated hypothesis still makes every finite-dimensional subspace of K^{1/p} weakly cartesian, by rescaling denominators and extending bounded functionals K-linearly; the Tate node holds for perfect k (monomial coefficient projections) and for rank one. Cases L=K and M=0 checked. No new node restates the item (D1). blueprint.via = [item] + item.via was checked, and every citation stays in unit sk-i-curve-zero, so no tool_uses are needed. rg -L found no duplicate in the DAG.
